_comment_v3350: v3.3.50: added PostHog analytics + session replay. Uses the module.no-external + posthog-recorder build (vendored locally under lib/posthog/) instead of the default bundle, which lazy-loads its rrweb recorder from PostHog's CDN via dynamic import() and ships it as a base64-encoded blob -- both flagged by Web Store review (dynamic remote code is disallowed under MV3, and the encoded blob reads as obfuscated code). Session replay only runs on the sidepanel (posthog-init.js, a module script -- popup.html was skipped since it's open a few seconds at most and eagerly loading ~560KB of recorder JS there isn't worth the added open-latency). The background service worker has no window/document at all, so it posts extension_installed/extension_updated events straight to PostHog's capture HTTP endpoint instead of using the SDK. distinct_id is synced through chrome.storage.local (the one storage area MV3 shares across every extension context) so both paths identify the same install. Login/chat-input fields are masked via maskAllInputs; already-sent chat bubbles remain visible in replays.
_comment_v3349: v3.3.49: version-only bump so a new Chrome Web Store submission has a strictly higher version than the 3.3.48 already live there (Web Store rejected a same-version re-upload). No functional changes since 3.3.48.
_comment_v3348: v3.3.48: adds a Patience slider below the model picker, matching the desktop app's v3.2.75 feature. A new 'Auto (Patience)' model entry ranks installed local Ollama models by size (fast<->capable) and picks along the slider's position, or hands off to 'distributed' (NVIDIA PAIR) at high patience when PAIR is actually connected with paired nodes. Fixes a real bug found while adding this: the literal string 'auto' could reach the server's /chat/stream unresolved, producing '[Note: model 'auto' is not installed on this server - using ... instead]' -- the picker value is now always resolved (resolveEffectiveModel) to a real model name before a request is ever sent.
_comment_v3347: v3.3.47: the 'thinking' indicator's elapsed-wait display showed raw seconds (e.g. '142s'), unlike the desktop app's wait timer which has always formatted this as minutes+seconds ('2m 22s') via _fmt_mmss -- confirmed as a real gap when asked whether the extension matches the desktop app's features. Ported the same formatting (fmtMmSs in sidepanel.js) so a long wait reads the same way in both places.
_comment_v3346: v3.3.46: version-only bump so a new Chrome Web Store submission has a strictly higher version than the 3.3.45 already live there. No functional changes since 3.3.45.
_comment_v3345: v3.3.45: security hardening from a pen-test pass. The Chat History panel's conversation id was concatenated raw into a data-id="..." attribute when rebuilding the history list -- ids are normally an internally-generated timestamp+random string, but if a malformed one ever reached chrome.storage (a sync bug, a corrupted entry) it could break out of the attribute and inject markup. Now escaped like every other dynamic value in that panel (model names, account info, tool-call JSON were already escaped in a prior pass).
_comment_v3344: v3.3.44: two fixes. (1) usage/spend recorded while using the extension against a local SurfiAI-Server (127.0.0.1:8080) never reached the account dashboard, even signed in -- only the desktop app pushed its local usage ledger on login. pullAccountSyncOnLogin now also pushes this device's local /api/cloud/kpi daily rows to /auth/kpi/push on sign-in. (2) the agent loop's 'keep going' problem: a routine, recoverable failure (Anthropic 529 Overloaded, a rate limit, a 5xx the server had already retried) was misclassified as permanent, so the agent gave up after one 1.5s retry and needed a manual follow-up message every time, even though just retrying always worked. Root cause was two compounding bugs in isTransientFailure() -- its HTTP-status regex was delimited by literal backspace bytes instead of \b word-boundary escapes (silently never matched anything), and the in-stream {error:...} path never recorded the failure text for it to check in the first place. Both fixed, plus 529/overloaded/rate-limit added to the recognized patterns. Long agent runs should no longer stall on transient provider overload.
_comment_v3321: v3.3.21: split-view detection fixed. v3.3.19/3.3.20 detected a split by querying tabs with active:true, assuming a split marks both halves active. Chromium marks exactly one tab per window active (Tab.active == TabModel::IsActivated()), so the query always returned one tab and the entire split feature â€” pane context and {pane:N} tool routing â€” was unreachable. Detection now uses Tab.splitViewId (Chrome 140+), with Tab.highlighted as a fallback.
_comment_v335: v3.3.5: removed manifest `key` and `oauth2` â€” Google SSO now runs through the surfiai.com WP bridge in a normal tab, so the extension ID no longer matters and chrome.identity is unused. Removing the key also lets this side-loaded copy coexist with the (old) Web Store install instead of colliding on the same ID.
